candidates.text:
this is quite an interesting essay from a deepseek engineer and it may highlight one area where openai and anthropic significantly disagree, at least publicly:

openai has tried very hard to give people access to the most powerful models on the order of weeks or months from their creation. I very much doubt there will be a time when this is not true. i believe sam and greg would rather shut down the organization than be some sort of a SaaS company that model access to a small set of trusted companies, it’s not in their DNA. they have made choices that are negative EV to the business to pursue broad access like a utility , decisions that even may make OpenAI non competitive with anthropic in certain long run scenarios. it is my assumption that powerful models will be accessible to billions as long as we can keep training models safely

the EAs probably disagree with me but I believe this is basically consistent with the practice of AI safety. the vast majority of risks are from the creation of the model and not from its deployment. “misuse” is far less bad and much easier to detect and contain over time than “existential risk”. it is relatively much easier to find terrorists and so forth using the product to create pandemics than it is to find a misaligned ASI that’s actively trying to evade your monitoring and control

(also I am obviously not endorsing this fellow’s opinion of dario or anthropic, but this is a very interesting look into a compelling anti lab sentiment)

candidates.text: RT @kapoorkkunal: We have a national cleanliness mission and a political class that treats every pole and street light, as a personal billb…

‘Attention Is All You Need’ is the whitepaper that unlocked the AI cycle. 

Much of what followed has been duct tape. 

I don’t mean that as an insult. Duct tape built half the modern world.

Consider two of the most important techniques driving AI forward today.

First: chain of reasoning.

Instead of asking the model to take one clean shot at an answer, we give it more inference time to decompose the problem, explore alternatives, check its work, and try again.

Step. Check. Revise.

Second: loops.

One model creates. Another evaluates. The first revises. 

The cycle continues until the output survives the critic.

At Meta, Muse is the public example. 

Meta’s AI chief noted that putting an eval LLM around a creator LLM, run the loop repeatedly, produce work comparable to that of a hundred engineers.

Impressive.

Also: It’s more MacGyver duct tape. 

That is what frontier AI increasingly looks like. 

So why do the models keep improving?

Scale.

More data. More parameters. More training compute. More inference compute. Better chips. Better post-training.

The breakthroughs have lagged the expectations.

Another reason AI leaders are saying ‘time to slow down’ is not the catastrophe risk which is nonsense. It is that expectations are being lowered and managed.

Root Cause: The brightest minds in the AI research world - Ilya, Murati, Dean are all raising gobs of capital instead of doing research that sparked the initial breakthru.

Last but not the least… ❤️

Jab ye cohort start hua tha, honestly AI ki duniya bahut badi aur abstract lagti thi. Bahut saari cheezein samajh nahi aati thi aur kaafi doubts the.

But these 2.5 months changed that.

Cohort ke saath-saath bahut saare doubts clear hue, naye concepts seekhe, aur AI ko thoda better samajhne laga. Bahut kuch banaya, bahut kuch bigada 😂, aur usse bhi zyada cheezein try ki.

Sabse interesting cheez jo seekhi — AI is nothing but a next-token predictor. Ek simple concept, but uske around kitni badi duniya build ho sakti hai, ye samajhna kaafi amazing tha.

In 2.5 months, sirf AI ke concepts nahi seekhe, balki actually cheezein build karne ka confidence bhi aaya.

Aaj batch officially complete ho gaya hai, but honestly, product aana abhi baaki hai. 😄

Thank you @Hiteshdotcom,@piyushgarg_dev @nirudhuuu ,@yntpdotme,@surajtwt_ , @BlazeisCoding all mentors for guiding us throughout this journey, doubts clear karne ke liye, aur har session ko interesting banane ke liye. ❤️

And a big thank you to @ChaiCodeHQ for creating this cohort and bringing all of us together.

See you all on the other side! ❤️

In early-stage startups, truth-seeking behaviors are a lot more complex and uncomfortable than consensus-seeking and blame-shifting behaviors. 

You will have team members try to assign fault to someone else and shift blame rather than take responsibility and find the truth about what's broken. 

..or worse, trying to find a way that everyone is comfortable and okay with. 

A business is like an organism, ur job is to take feedback directly from the sensory organs closest to the actions (fingers, eyes, ears etc) 

Middle management needs to understand what is temporary and futile and what is important enough to escalate, and the leadership needs to talk extensively to those in the field and act on them.
